name: Brady Quinn
strengths: Quinn operates from a compact platform and delivers on time to the intermediate windows.
Quinn creates when the first read is covered — enough mobility to extend without turning into a pure runner.
Quinn keeps his eyes downfield after the snap and does not panic when the pocket shrinks.
weaknesses: Quinn still needs to prove he can drive the deep out consistently from a 6-0 frame versus taller SEC edges.
comparison: Quinn comps to Bryce Young — 6-0 compact creator who wins with timing, eyes, and enough mobility to extend plays without becoming a pure runner.
projection: Quinn projects as a Year 2–3 campus starter (develop and compete Year 1). Ceiling: multi-year SEC starter — the compact timing QB who can take the keys once the processing stays ahead of the rush.
schemeFit: Quinn fits a timing / progression QB room that values eyes and create ability over pure prototype height.
insiderNotes: Quinn is a compact 6-0 Chaminade-Madonna QB who wins with timing, eyes, and enough create ability to extend plays. Platform stays clean in the intermediate game. Wins with processing and composure — a pocket-progression mold who can still scramble when needed.
